question.text: Consider the parabola $y^{2}=4 x$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on the parabola where $P(4,-4)$ and $Q (9,6)$. Let $R$ be a point on the arc of the parabola between $P$ and $Q$. Then, the area of $\Delta P Q R$ is largest when

solution.text: Let $\quad f(x)=x \log x+x-3$ $\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=x \cdot \frac{1}{x}+\log x+1$ $\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=\log x+2>0$ $\Rightarrow f(1)=-2$ and $f(3)=3 \log 3, f(1) \cdot f(3 < 0)$ Hence, exactly one root in $x \in(1,3)$ as $f(x)>0$ Equation of $P Q$ is $2 x-y=12$ Perpendicular distance $A R=\left|\frac{2 t^{2}-2 t-12}{\sqrt{5}}\right|=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}(t-3 \cdot(t+4)$ $A R$ is Maximum, at $t=\frac{1}{2}$ $\therefore R$ is $\left(\frac{1}{4}, 1\right)$
